title: URL import probes every two-segment path as a git repo; a false verdict poisons the host
description: git::detect_target shape-parses any https://host/a/b as owner/repo and, for unknown hosts, runs an 8s git ls-remote before page capture — so every ordinary web import on a new host paid that probe (git_hosts.json is full of alaskaair.com, sfpl.org, t-mobile.com…). ferrariclubofamerica.org/page/MembershipMain got a TRUE verdict, and the import then tried to clone over ssh (port 22 timeout) and landed as an error source. Fix: a bare owner/repo shape on a host without a forge-looking label (github, gitlab, gitea, git, code, scm…) is not probed; explicit /blob/ and /tree/ paths still are. Workaround in the field: add the URL with a #fragment so the shape parser skips it.
close_reason: Implemented on cld/mcp-import-feedback, PR #39; awaiting in-app pass before merge

title: Background sweep yields to foreground chat on Ollama's queue
description: Ollama serves one request per model at a time (OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1 default). The gist/section/tag sweep issues back-to-back Small-role calls (3-4 s each, see ~/.ollama/logs/server.log 2026-09-01 23:10), so a foreground helper (gap query, outline pick, Ai::helpers 10 s ceiling) queues behind them and times out — observed live: gapMs 10001 on a healthy server. Fix: a foreground-in-flight flag the sweep checks between calls (pause while any chat/helper call is open), or a small warm second Ollama slot. Measure: gap stage under 3 s while a sweep runs.
close_reason: Fixed on cld/sweep-yields: foreground guard (chat, deep research, ask-everything, generate) + Ai::background() waits before each Small call. Measured gap stage 10002 ms → 3806 ms with a sweep in flight; 663 ms idle. Cross-process (installed app + dev app on one store) is out of scope.

title: Incremental FTS optimize ranks differently (and non-deterministically) vs a from-scratch index
description: Found while measuring RFC-outline-index phase 2 (2026-09-01). Seeding rows after an existing FTS index, then flush_fts (the optimize/delta path), gave run-to-run flips on a BM25-dependent query (topic MRR 0.73 vs 0.75, one query found/missed) and different numbers than create_index --replace over the same rows (MRR 0.79, stable). Production uses the incremental path after every import. Verify whether the delta index merges lag or score differently; consider a periodic from-scratch rebuild (e.g. in db maintenance) or checking lance-index behaviour for optimize on FTS.

title: Events: feeds, watchers, arrivals, live cards, agent stream
description: Alchemy has the consumer half of an event system (source_events, change-triggered standing questions, Weave, Brief, list_source_events) and almost no producers: the only event kind is 'updated' and it fires only on re-fetch of already-imported pages. This epic adds producers (feed sources with autodiscovery, a real event vocabulary, per-URL watch cadence, FSEvents for the open notebook, item-level Mac events via cider) and surfaces (trigger filters on reports, an Arrivals strip, live answer cards, an SSE/MCP stream for agents) under strict cost rules: events never call a model directly. Design: docs/RFC-events.md. Survey (2026-09-01): 285 URL sources across 14 notebooks, 31 pages advertise feeds, 15 domains have well-known-path feeds.
notes: cld/events + PR #47, all six phases. 2026-09-02 evening: cider 0.6.2 pinned from crates.io (library logs via log facade; diagnostics::install_log_bridge routes to note!). macwatch uses watch_via(Via::Auto) with a fallback to Via::Fsevents — the bridge CLI installed but denied Calendar access fails cider's joined watch, FSEvents half included (seen live in the dev app). Duplicate Reminders 'added' root cause: the write-back's Source snapshot predates cider's multi-second write, so the watch resyncs first and the write-back diffs against its stale copy; resync_mac_source now re-reads the row under the scan lock. app_state kv table + robots.rs landed earlier. Releasing as v0.54.0.
close_reason: Shipped in v0.54.0: all six RFC-events phases, app_state kv, robots.txt, cider 0.6.2 log bridge, FSEvents fallback, single item events

title: Dev builds clobber the shared MCP discovery file
description: Dev instances bind mcp_port+1 (41415) to avoid colliding with the installed app, but both write the same <app-data>/mcp.json. A dev run rewrites it to 41415; after the dev app quits, the CLI and agents discover a dead port until the installed app restarts (hit live 2026-08-31: CLI errored against 41415 while nothing listened; installed app relaunch fixed it). Options: dev builds write mcp.dev.json and leave mcp.json alone, or discovery consumers fall back to the default port when the recorded pid is dead. Discovery already records pid.
close_reason: Fixed on main cabac45: dev builds write/remove mcp.dev.json instead of clobbering mcp.json; CLAUDE.md documents ALCHEMY_MCP_DISCOVERY for aiming the CLI at a dev build. Gates green; live run blocked by a concurrent pre-fix dev instance from another worktree (which demonstrated the bug once more).
